documents.directions: Answer each question. Calculators are allowed.

questions.skill: which calculation gives a conditional percent

prompt.A: A school surveyed students about their grade and whether they joined a club. Of the 9th graders, what percent joined a club? Which calculation answers the question?

figure.A: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360 96" width="360" height="96" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13"><text x="8" y="20" font-weight="bold">Grade</text><text x="120" y="20" font-weight="bold">Joined a club</text><text x="250" y="20" font-weight="bold">Did not join</text><text x="8" y="50">9th grade</text><text x="150" y="50">36</text><text x="280" y="50">24</text><text x="8" y="80">10th grade</text><text x="150" y="80">30</text><text x="280" y="80">50</text></svg>

A: Divide 36 by 140, the total of everyone surveyed
Divide 36 by 60, the total of the 9th graders surveyed
Divide 36 by 66, the total who joined a club
Divide 60 by 140, the share of 9th graders surveyed

why.A: The "of" group is the 9th graders, so their total (60) is the denominator and the 9th graders who joined (36) are the numerator.

prompt.A: A coach finds the least-squares line $\hat{y} = 38.5 + 2.3x$, where $x$ is hours of practice per week and $\hat{y}$ is the predicted free-throw percent. Which statement interprets the slope?

A: Each extra hour of weekly practice adds about 2.3 predicted points
A player who does not practice is predicted to make 2.3% of free throws
The correlation between weekly practice hours and free-throw percent is about 2.3
Players whose free-throw percent is 2.3 points higher are predicted to practice one more hour a week

why.A: The slope, 2.3, is the change in predicted free-throw percent for each one-hour increase in weekly practice.

prompt.A: A ranger measured young trees aged 3 to 9 years. The least-squares line is $\hat{y} = 2.4 + 1.9x$, where $x$ is age in years and $\hat{y}$ is predicted height in feet. Predict the height of a tree that is 6 years old.

why.A: ŷ = 2.4 + 1.9(6) = 13.8 ft. Age 6 is inside the ages measured, so the prediction is reasonable.

fields.prompt: A ranger measured young trees aged {{lo}} to {{hi}} years. The least-squares line is $\hat{y} = {{c0}} + {{m}}x$, where $x$ is age in years and $\hat{y}$ is predicted height in feet. Predict the height of a tree that is {{x0}} years old.
fields.why: ŷ = {{c0}} + {{m}}({{x0}}) = {{c0 + m*x0|2}} ft. Age {{x0}} is inside the ages measured, so the prediction is reasonable.

questions.skill: strength of r versus its sign

prompt.A: Hours studied and quiz score have r = 0.74. Hours of TV watched and quiz score have r = −0.81. Which statement is correct?

A: Because 0.74 is above 0 and −0.81 is below 0, the study relationship is the stronger one
Because one r is positive and one is negative, 0.74 and −0.81 can't be compared for their strength
Because −0.81 is farther from 0 than 0.74 is, the TV relationship is the stronger of the two
Because a negative r shows a weaker pattern, the TV relationship at −0.81 is the weaker one

why.A: Strength is how far r is from 0: |−0.81| = 0.81 is more than 0.74, so the TV relationship is stronger (and negative).

fields.prompt: Hours studied and quiz score have r = {{rs}}. Hours of TV watched and quiz score have r = {{-rt|u}}. Which statement is correct?
choices: Because {{rs}} is above 0 and {{-rt|u}} is below 0, the study relationship is the stronger one
Because one r is positive and one is negative, {{rs}} and {{-rt|u}} can't be compared for their strength
Because {{-rt|u}} is farther from 0 than {{rs}} is, the TV relationship is the stronger of the two
Because a negative r shows a weaker pattern, the TV relationship at {{-rt|u}} is the weaker one
fields.why: Strength is how far r is from 0: |{{-rt|u}}| = {{rt}} is more than {{rs}}, so the TV relationship is stronger (and negative).

prompt.A: Researchers recorded hours of exercise per week and resting heart rate for 40 adults, to use exercise time to predict heart rate. Name the explanatory variable and the response variable.
prompt.B: A study recorded hours of sleep and reaction time for 30 drivers, to use sleep to predict reaction time. Name the explanatory variable and the response variable.
prompt.C: A stand recorded the daily high temperature and cups of lemonade sold on 25 days, to use temperature to predict sales. Name the explanatory variable and the response variable.

answer.A: Explanatory: hours of exercise per week. Response: resting heart rate.
answer.B: Explanatory: hours of sleep. Response: reaction time.
answer.C: Explanatory: daily high temperature. Response: cups of lemonade sold.

A: exercise is explanatory, heart rate is the response
B: sleep is explanatory, reaction time is the response
C: temperature is explanatory, lemonade sales are the response

why.A: The variable used to predict is explanatory (x); the one predicted is the response (y).
